text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING oncall (sev2) - tenant=acme-corp - tail latency spikes on dedicated pool acme-ded-1. Auto-alert triggered at 10:14 UTC.
Amanda L: Seeing very large queue depth for tenant acme-corp on acme-ded-1, p99 > 3s and backpressure on the scheduler. Multiple requests stuck in batching for >200ms. Impacting customer interactive features.
Leo K: I can repro the backlog in the dashboard - scheduler_queue_size for acme-corp is 78, avg batch formation time 250ms. CPU on the host is fine but GPU memory pressure creeping.
Miguel (oncall): Paging in. Oncall will take. Anyone already tried per-tenant throttles?
Amanda L: Not yet. Proposed immediate mitigation: reduce tenant max_batch_tokens and lower max_batch_size for acme-corp so batches are formed faster and fit memory, plus temporarily increase per-tenant concurrency to allow smaller batches to run in parallel.
Ryan: Agreed. Quick change via control-plane override: set `tenant_overrides` for acme-corp. I can apply a hotfix.
Amanda L: Steps: 1) apply override 2) monitor p99 3) if not improving, shift traffic to compatible smaller model variant (acme-llama-13b-8bit) 4) coordinate with acctops for customer notice.
Leo K: Here's the command I'm going to run (control plane API):

```bash
# PATCH tenant override
curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.dev/internal/tenants/acme-corp/overrides \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "inference_config": {
      "max_batch_tokens": 512,
      "max_batch_size": 4,
      "scheduler_delay_ms": 5,
      "max_inflight_requests": 8
    }
  }'
```

Amanda L: Applying now. Will report back in 60s.
incident-bot: Action logged - override applied by Leo K at 10:18 UTC.
Leo K: Done. Overrides are live for acme-corp.
Amanda L: Dashboard update: queue_size dropping from 78 -> 18, avg batch formation 60ms, p99 latency from 3.2s -> 680ms. GPU mem used down ~12%.
Miguel (oncall): Nice. Any downstream regressions? throughput per-second dropped ~15% but interactive latencies are acceptable.
Julia (acctops): Notifying the customer about a temporary performance tuning change and that we may schedule a maintenance window for a stable config. Drafting message now.
Ryan: One more tweak: let's also add a short lived per-tenant `rate_limit` to smooth spikes: `{ "rate_limit_rps": 40 }` - only if we see queue re-buildup.
Amanda L: Agreed. If queue climbs over 40 again we'll enable it.
Leo K: Logging snippet from node acme-node-3 right after change: `scheduler: formed_batch size=3 tokens=460 latency_ms=58 -> dispatched to gpu0`
Amanda L: Running quick smoke tests to ensure no OOMs. All good so far.
Miguel (oncall): Handoff note - I'll stay on this until 11:00 UTC, then hand to oncall next. Leave runbook steps in #oncall-runbooks.
Amanda L: Follow-ups captured: (1) post-incident followup to create a per-tenant autoscaling policy for acme-ded-1, (2) add a dashboard alert for `tenant_batch_formation_time > 150ms`, (3) evaluate lowering default `max_batch_tokens` for high-latency tenants.
Ryan: Long-term: implement adaptive batch sizing that considers queue depth + epoch mem pressure, and a safer default for dedicated pools with mixed-tenancy.
Julia (acctops): Customer message sent: "We've applied a temporary tuning change to reduce latency; you may see slightly lower throughput. We'll follow-up with a plan for a lasting fix." They acknowledged, asked to be kept in loop.
incident-bot: Incident updated to 'mitigated' at 10:45 UTC by Amanda L. Severity remains S2, postmortem required.
Miguel (oncall): Thanks team. I have notes and will create the incident ticket + assign postmortem owner (Amanda). Handing off to next oncall in 10m. :thumbsup:
Amanda L: will write up the brief timeline and root cause analysis starter: likely workload spike + conservative tenant batch config -> slow batch formation and queueing.
Ryan: Saved override in infra repo as `acme-corp-temp-tune` - will open PR to make it parameterized.
Leo K: Closing thread for now, will reopen if symptoms return.
Julia (acctops): Marking customer as "notified" in CRM and flagging for scheduled follow-up call.
Miguel (oncall): last note - for the postmortem include exact metrics: pre-change p99 3200ms, post-change p99 680ms, queue depth peak 78 -> steady 12.
Amanda L: Copy that. I'll include the exact dashboard links in the ticket.
